form.name: Form 22, Application for Permit To Drill, Deepen or Re-enter
form.notes: Read the fillable PDF (fetched with WebFetch, text extracted with pdftotext; file last modified 4 Apr 2016, printed revision R 10/09). Cites ARM 36.22.307 and 36.22.601. Submitted in quadruplicate to the Billings office; no online filing found on the operator page. Companion pages not read: APD process checklist (2018-APD-Process.pdf), Bond Overview, ARM 36.22.601 and 36.22.1308. The agency's main host bogc.dnrc.mt.gov is blocked by the sandbox proxy.

operator_type.n: No business-type box on Form 22; none in any source read

sources.tested: Folder listing 200 and 2026 folder 200: 42 weekly letters from 2026-01-09 (the 2025 and 2024 folders answer 200 with no files, so a 'since 2016' archive is not there). Each letter has the sections New Locations, New Locations - Horizontal Wells, Re-Issued Locations, Completions, Expired Permits and Abandoned Wells. The 403s the first research met on the bogfiles.dnrc.mt.gov host came from the backslashes in the listing's links (//WeeklyActivityLetter\20261023.pdf, sent as %5C): with a slash every file answers 200 and supports range requests. The 42 letters read with pdftotext hold 225 permit entries (219 unique); 218 of the 225 match an event of the Well History exactly, and the history has 14 approvals no letter lists. Used only as a check.

columns: MT_CompleteWellList.zip: one row per well, with a 'Permitted' date
activity_types: wells that still exist, with their permit date
sources.tested: Both zips read 2026-11-01 (1.8 MB for the well list). The well list holds only wells that still exist: its 'Permitted' years 2019 to 2025 give 49, 27, 34, 45, 45, 62, 59 against the Board's 79, 37, 41, 54, 58, 66, 62 (62% in 2019 up to 95% in 2025: expired and never-drilled permits are gone), which would draw a false rise; not used for permits. It is a good, cheap source for the wells themselves. The 403s of the first research came from backslash paths on the bogfiles host (with a slash the files answer 200).

notices of intent and subsequent reports
sources.tested: Driven and read 2026-11-01 the way the page does, four requests 3 s apart: GET the page; POST the choice of the date field (the page posts back to offer 'Prior To / Equal To / After'); POST the search 'Date Approved After 12/31/2018' with the Search button; GET Export.aspx?type=csv, which works only in the session that searched (the session cookie is held in memory). About 4.4 MB, 19,800 events, 1,089 of them permits, 16 seconds; two real runs gave byte-identical output. The Dataminer sits behind an F5 BIG-IP application firewall: it answered the research proxy with no challenge or refusal, and a datacenter address might get one.

grade_reason: The Board's Dataminer Well History page lists every event on every well (permits, notices of intent, completions, spuds, plugging, expiry dates) with a Date Approved and a type of work, and offers the whole result as a CSV export: free, no login, with county, well type and operator. Held to B, not A: the export is a form-driven download inside a session behind a firewall (four requests, no documented interface), and the well type and the operator are the well's today. The weekly letters cover only 2026. Updated 2026-11-01: a producer reads the export each week; its permits to drill, re-entries and horizontals match the Board's annual reviews exactly for 2019 to 2023 (79, 37, 41, 54, 58) and are one short in 2024 (66 against 67), and its re-issued permits match in all six years.
producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_mt.py. Drives the Dataminer Well History form as the page does, four requests 3 s apart (GET the page; POST the choice of the date field; POST the search 'Date Approved After 12/31/2018' with the Search button; GET Export.aspx?type=csv in the same session, cookie held in memory), about 4.4 MB and 19,800 events each run, 16 s; nothing is kept from the committed file, so a corrected date is picked up the next week. Counts every permit event by month of Dt_Effect. Bands from Typ_Work: 'Permit to Drill' and 'Permit to Drill, Horizontal' = new, unless the well's type is a service well (inj); re-enter, redrill or deepen, horizontal re-drill and new laterals = redrill; re-permit, permit modification and correction = amend (a re-issue is the same well again); rework and other are null (recompletions and plug-backs are sundry notices, not permits). A permit type it does not know fails the run. Only date, work type, well type, county and operator are read from a row; API number, well name, field, location, status and the free-text comment never are, and the export is never written. A lag of 7 days. A 403 exits 2 and keeps last week's file.
privacy_notes: The letters, the export and the layer name operators (companies in the files read); the export's free-text comment can hold names and phone numbers and is never read. Form 22 collects an operator address and phone and a signing agent; the surface owner is not named on the form. Nothing copied.
